The staged `poc` is 49,780 bytes, so the harness clips it to `size = 32768`, copies only that prefix into global `static_data[32768]`, and passes the copied bytes into project code. The copied tail still contains quotes through offset 32767.

Source. The fuzz-only helper consumes the copied buffer and clipped length and reduces the logical parser span to `len - 1`. On the witnessed path, the project lexer will parse 32,767 bytes even though 32,768 copied bytes exist.

The lexer state is materialized as `pos = start = static_data` and `end = static_data + 32767`. Byte `static_data[32767]` is therefore a copied slack byte outside the logical parser span but still inside the backing array.

While `parse_key_value()` is requesting the next value token, `lex_config()` reaches the clipped tail. In the saved witness, bytes 32723-32767 are all `0x22`, so when `next()` consumes the quote at offset 32765, `lexer->pos` advances to offset 32766 and the line-460 2-byte probe sees quotes at offsets 32766-32767. That admits a final opening `"""` at offsets 32765-32767, with offset 32767 being the single copied slack byte beyond `lexer->end`.

`peek(lexer)` sees `"` at offset 32766, so `end` becomes `"""`. `advance_n(2)` then consumes the remaining opening quotes at offsets 32766 and 32767 and moves `lexer->pos` and `lexer->start` to `static_data + 32768`, one byte past the copied array, before the loop body tests for a terminator.

Root cause. The loop's first action is still `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)`. No guard proves `lexer->end - lexer->pos >= 3`, so this path can probe three bytes even after `advance_n(2)` has already moved `lexer->pos` past the copied buffer. Local repository history commit `604eb733ecdbe8f637787825223c4c4ba5a3459c` fixes this site by adding `if (remaining(lexer) < 3) break;` immediately before this line.
